idiom_name: closed hierarchy: one declaration naming the cases + one immutable carrier per case + a total eliminator
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare one abstract type as the union and give it no state; declare every alternative as a final immutable data type carrying exactly its own fields; construct values only through per-case constructors that set discriminant and payload together; and consume the union with one elimination construct whose branches map one-to-one onto the cases, written without a catch-all arm. Close the set wherever the language allows it (sealed/permits keyword, same-file or same-package rules, an unexported marker method, a private supertrait, a union alias checked by a type checker) and, where it does not, add the strongest mechanical check the toolchain offers - a `-Wswitch-enum` build flag, a linter, or an external checker - plus one raising default arm as the runtime backstop. Keep the base free of shared fields and behaviour so the sum cannot silently degenerate into a tag plus a record.
code_sketch:
union Payment =                     # sealed where the notation allows it
    case Card(number: string)
    case Transfer(iban: string)

function describe(p: Payment) -> string:
    match p:                        # total: every case named, no catch-all
        Card(number)   -> number
        Transfer(iban) -> iban
pitfalls: Adding a case while a catch-all arm exists: the change compiles everywhere and the new case is silently mishandled.
Sharing state or behaviour on the base type turns the closed sum back into a tag plus a record.
Immutability that stops at the reference: mutable collections behind the case fields reappear as illegal states and break value equality.

Publishing a sealed type without an explicit unknown or non-exhaustive path: adding a case breaks external exhaustive consumers or compiled matches; instead use `#[non_exhaustive]`, an `Unknown` case, or a documented major-version change.

Wrong move: encoding the case discriminator in storage or on the wire as the case's declaration position (enum `ordinal()`, variant index) -> inserting a case in the middle silently renumbers every previously persisted value and old records deserialize into the wrong case -> carry a stable tag instead (Java enum serialization stores the constant name, never the ordinal; Effective Java item 35 warns that ordinals are brittle) and parse it through one total boundary parser.

Wrong move: letting a recursive case reference the sum type directly (`Cons(value, next)` with `next` typed as the sealed type itself) -> the carrier has no finite representation and the compiler rejects the declaration (Rust: an enum variant holding `List` directly has infinite size) -> put the recursive field behind an indirection: `Box<List>`, Swift `indirect case`, or a boxed child node.

Wrong move: scattering the cases across packages, modules or plugin jars and assuming the compiler's closure tracks them -> the language's scope rule rejects the declaration (Kotlin requires direct subclasses in the same package and module, Scala 2 in the same source file), and moving a case out to make it pluggable silently reopens the hierarchy -> keep the base and all cases in one compilation unit, and model a genuinely open boundary as an open interface rather than a sealed sum.
